t: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the Federal interest in dredging the mouth of the Choctawhatchee River, Florida, to remove the sand plug.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a study of a local Florida river project implies coordination with state or local interests. The text does not say so: it only directs the Secretary, a federal official, to conduct a study on the Federal interest. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any non-federal party is mentioned, and a study is not itself a decision with outside participation.
fable.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the Federal interest in dredging the mouth of the Choctawhatchee River, Florida, to remove the sand plug.

qwen_block.w: This section mandates a study by the Secretary but does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any parties outside the federal government. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or coordination with state/local entities. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the Federal interest in dredging the mouth of the Choctawhatchee River, Florida, to remove the sand plug.

opus.w: The section only tells the Secretary, a federal official, to study whether there is a Federal interest in dredging the mouth of the Choctawhatchee River. It names no state, local, tribal, expert or public participant and creates no comment period, hearing, committee, rulemaking power or right to sue. The Florida location might suggest local involvement, but the text requires none, and even a study done with outside experts would not count, as Example 3 shows.

But the section names no outside party: no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory panel, rulemaking or right to sue. Only the Secretary acts, so nothing crosses the federal boundary.

qwen_chat.w: The section mandates that the Secretary conduct a study, but it does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any parties outside the federal government. The definition of participation requires that the federal government consult or coordinate with people outside the government (such as states, tribes, the public, or experts) before making a decision. Since the text only describes an internal study by the Secretary without specifying any external involvement, it does not meet the criteria for participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the Federal interest in dredging the mouth of the Choctawhatchee River, Florida, to remove the sand plug.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that a "study" implies gathering input from outside experts or the public, thus constituting participation. However, the text itself does not mandate any consultation, comment period, or advisory board involving non-federal entities. It simply directs the Secretary to conduct a study. Without explicit language requiring interaction with outsiders, this is an internal executive action.
